dedupe_keys.name: nmecr building energy measurement and verification

description: nmecr is a Python toolbox for modelling building energy use in measurement and verification work. Its repository lists eleven algorithms for hourly, daily or monthly consumption profiles and provides examples for commercial and institutional buildings. Users supply metered energy, weather and operating context; outputs include a baseline model and estimated savings or expected use for a selected site. Geographic coverage follows the building records supplied. The README documents the supported algorithms, and GitHub metadata states MIT licensing. A limitation is that a fitted baseline may reflect occupancy or operational changes that are not measured, so estimated savings depend on the chosen comparison period and covariates. nmecr can calibrate demand and retrofit scenarios in building-energy or district infrastructure simulations. The related catalogue ERA5 record supplies weather variables, not a building-use baseline. No utility bills or Python package were downloaded.
